source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BMC Web UI and navigate to the Network protocol properties page.
2. Check text displayed and make sure it is readable.
3. Enable DDNS.
4. Under Method, choose Use domain name obtained from the DHCP server.
You may need to click on the DNS tab and enter in the IP of the DNS server.
5. Click Apply on the DDNS tab.
If it cannot connect to the domain server, it should show that it is unable to pull the domain name.
If it does not pull the domain name and it cannot connect to the server but does not show that it cannot pull the domain name, this is a defect.
6. After the domain name resolves, select the option to Use custom domain name.
7. Enter in the domain name to be sent to the server.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. DDNS information should be displayed correctly.
2. The domain name should resolve after step5

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -iE "IP Address|MAC"; echo ---nslookup---; nslookup "$BMC_HOSTNAME" 8.8.8.8 2>&1 | head -10; echo ---lan-dns---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -i dns
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the BMC `lan print` DNS/IP lines plus an `nslookup` of the BMC hostname against a resolver, so the user confirms the DDNS domain name resolves after enabling.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: DDNS registration requires the BMC to reach a working dynamic-DNS server/DHCP-issued domain; Web UI enablement is operator-side, agent verifies the resulting resolution from a client.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes the dependency on a DDNS/DNS environment, but only queries a public recursive resolver and never proves BMC-originated update, authoritative ownership, DHCP-domain selection, custom-domain handling or the mandatory unreachable-server UI error. It also exposes the BMC password and assumes channel/cipher semantics.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly separates provider, DHCP/custom domains, negative path, record identity and cleanup. This review retains its classification and makes explicit that custom-domain Apply/acceptance is absent from the Master Criteria.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 828/2291 repeats the public `nslookup` and command-present framing without validating authoritative registration, cached answers, update credentials, negative UI behavior or cleanup.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-992 draft was inspected only as history. It under-classified the hybrid case as MANUAL ONLY even though authoritative DNS queries, provider logs, TTL and record cleanup are material automated evidence.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 preserves writable DDNS and both source methods rather than reducing to read-only queries; ED-36 treats provider/domain/credential details as readiness inputs; ED-38 requires approval and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify readable BMC WebUI DDNS information, successful DHCP-provided-domain registration/resolution after Apply, an explicit failure message when the domain service is unreachable, and the separately entered custom-domain path without conflating those outcomes.
original_method: In an isolated authorized DNS/DDNS environment, an operator uses the WebUI to enable DDNS and select the DHCP-provided domain, applies it, observes either successful authoritative registration or the required failure message, then selects and enters a custom domain. Authoritative queries and server/BMC logs correlate each result to the exact BMC.
manual_activity: A qualified operator approves the registration, confirms WebUI readability and exact failure message, performs the DHCP-domain and custom-domain selections, and authorizes cleanup. Automation may query authoritative servers, correlate provider/update logs, measure TTL propagation and verify or remove the approved test record.
required_inputs: Immutable BMC/firmware/interface/MAC/IP/hostname identity and supported DDNS methods, address families and record types
Isolated DHCP option/domain behavior, authoritative DDNS/DNS server and test zone, update protocol, allowed hostname/custom FQDN, expected A/AAAA or other RDATA and TTL
Protected update authentication/TSIG or vendor credential policy, BMC-to-server reachability, authoritative query endpoint and recursion/cache controls

Separate matrix for DHCP-derived positive success, controlled unreachable-server negative behavior and custom-domain Apply/registration/readback; the Master omits an explicit custom Apply/Criteria and Project SPEC must supply it before claiming that branch
Expected UI labels/error text or error identifier, timing/propagation windows, prior settings, alternate access, rollback and authorized record cleanup
safety_requirements: Use only an owned isolated test zone and approved names. Do not publish BMC management addresses into public or shared production DNS or overwrite an existing record.
Do not substitute `8.8.8.8` or another public recursive resolver for the authoritative Project service. A recursive answer may be cached, stale or unrelated to the current BMC update.
Correlate the record to the BMC MAC/IP/hostname, authoritative serial/timestamp and update log; a matching string alone does not prove the BMC created it.
Protect BMC and DDNS update credentials; never pass literal secrets with `-P` or log TSIG/authentication material. Rotate credentials if exposure occurs.

Run positive and negative paths as separately controlled conditions. Do not disable shared DNS infrastructure to create the negative path; isolate the BMC route/service or use an approved nonresponsive test endpoint.
Do not credit the custom-domain branch merely because text was entered. Require Project-defined Apply, persistence, authoritative registration and cleanup criteria before that branch can pass.

Do not automatically retry updates because duplicate transactions can hide timing/error behavior. Stop on unauthorized record, wrong RDATA, management loss, credential exposure or cleanup failure; restore prior settings and remove only the authorized test record.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, validate ownership, DHCP/custom name matrix, update protocol, authoritative query strategy, negative isolation and cleanup without modifying DUT or DNS state.
After operator actions, collect BMC/update-server/audit timestamps and authoritative nonrecursive answers, then correlate name, RDATA, TTL and identity for each approved branch.
Keep UI display/readability, DHCP-derived success, negative UI error and custom-domain registration as distinct checkpoints; do not let one satisfy another.
Do not choose or register a name, expose credentials, create an unapproved outage, retry automatically or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the isolated DDNS provider/zone, names, update credentials, three-branch acceptance, negative method, timing and cleanup.
Perform/observe the WebUI method selections, Apply and exact error/readability checkpoints; define the missing custom-domain Apply/Criteria in Project SPEC.
Restore prior DDNS/DNS/hostname state, authorize test-record deletion and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The resolver-query idea is useful only after registration, but the literal command neither configures DDNS nor queries the authoritative Project service. It uses unapproved public recursion, cannot distinguish stale data, omits UI/negative/custom paths, assumes channel/cipher and exposes the password.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved WebUI/API with protected credentials, provider/update logs and authoritative nonrecursive queries for the exact DHCP-derived and custom FQDNs. Exact commands depend on the authorized DDNS implementation and must include safe record cleanup.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: WebUI readability, DDNS enable, DHCP-provided domain, Apply, unreachable-server message, custom-domain entry, no Script and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Snapshot state; verify the controlled negative message; restore reachability and apply the DHCP-derived name; correlate authoritative registration; exercise the Project-completed custom-domain Apply/registration checkpoint; clean records and restore settings.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BMC DDNS client, DHCP service, authoritative test zone/provider and WebUI implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, browser, DHCP/DNS/DDNS server, update protocol and query-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform BMC DDNS specification, Project DHCP/domain plan and authoritative DNS provider/update policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds separate positive/negative/custom checkpoints, authoritative rather than public recursive proof, record ownership/TTL and deterministic cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A public `nslookup` does not prove BMC update; a correct record does not prove the required UI error; entering a custom name without Apply/authoritative evidence does not prove custom DDNS.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Provider/zone, names/RDATA/TTL, credentials, branch criteria, UI error, timing, recovery and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong or stale DDNS records can redirect management access, expose internal addressing or persist beyond the test.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC must complete the custom-domain Apply and acceptance semantics and may select vendor-supported update tooling, but must preserve the original DHCP-derived, failure-message and custom-entry checkpoints and record any unverified branch.
expected_evidence: BMC/firmware/MAC/IP/hostname identity, prior DDNS state and approved DHCP/domain/provider/zone/RDATA/TTL/credential plan
Readable WebUI baseline plus method/field screenshots or exports for DHCP-derived and custom-domain selections
Controlled unreachable-service condition and exact UI error/timestamp, followed by restored provider reachability
BMC/provider update logs and authoritative nonrecursive answer/TTL correlated to the BMC for the DHCP-derived name
Project-defined custom Apply/persistence plus authoritative record evidence, or an explicit NOT EXECUTED/coverage-gap status if not defined
Restored BMC settings, authorized record cleanup, stable access, retained logs and engineer-owned verdict per checkpoint

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source describes compatible positive, negative and custom-domain paths. It omits custom-domain Apply/Criteria detail, but that checkpoint can be completed by Project SPEC without changing the clear core DDNS purpose; it must not be credited until defined.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The DHCP-domain success and negative UI behavior are clear, and the custom branch has an identifiable readiness gap rather than irreconcilable semantics. Provider, records, credentials and custom acceptance are supplyable inputs.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects public-recursive-only proof and restores BMC update, UI error, custom-domain and cleanup coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation while explicitly preventing the underspecified custom branch from receiving automatic credit.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-exists reasoning with authoritative registration and branch-specific evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Changes MANUAL ONLY to package/user confirmation because server/query/log automation materially proves DDNS behavior while UI acceptance remains manual.

review_improvement: Prevents cached public DNS or a pre-existing record from falsely passing BMC DDNS and preserves the required failure message and incomplete custom-domain branch as separately visible coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: DDNS acceptance requires causality: the BMC must initiate an authorized update that produces the expected authoritative record. A recursive query alone lacks that causality. At the same time, the UI failure message and custom-domain workflow are distinct state transitions, so a hybrid evidence package is necessary and no single successful lookup can pass the whole case.
